_meta.description: Tool library metadata and substitutability equivalence relations

domains.information_retrieval: Tools that fetch information from external sources (web, news, academic, image, translation, summarization)
domains.computation: Tools that perform calculations, statistics, sorting, or numeric transformations
domains.communication: Tools that send messages via email, SMS, push notifications, or chat
domains.file_io: Tools that interact with the local filesystem
domains.scheduling: Tools that handle date/time operations and calendar events
domains.data_database: Tools that query, transform, or write to structured data stores (SQL, CSV, JSON)
domains.image_vision: Tools that process or analyze images (resize, crop, classify, OCR)
domains.audio_speech: Tools that handle audio input/output (transcription, synthesis, classification)

equivalence_groups.rationale: All return list of results for a query. Schema differs (different param names, different return shapes) but semantically equivalent for general-purpose information lookup.
Both send external messages with body content. Different protocol (email vs SMS). For substitutability tests on short messages only.
Both retrieve rows matching a condition from structured data (SQL database vs CSV file). Different query language but same semantic outcome.
Both analyze an image to extract structured information (category label vs text content). Different output shape but same underlying computer-vision capability.
Both deliver a short notification to a user/channel. Slack posts to a chat channel; push sends to a device. Same semantic intent: alert the recipient.
Both operate on calendar events. calendar_add creates an event; calendar_list queries events. Both are calendar CRUD operations over the same data store.
